sources.permission_evidence: Rechecked 2026-10-31 against the Court's official policy (last updated May 2026): https://cc.gov.eg/terms. The policy requires a personal account created by the Court and a current subscription for content access; permits viewing/copying only for legal, academic, research and documentation purposes; prohibits commercial use or republication without prior written approval; does not authorize automated/bulk extraction; it expressly prohibits automated or bulk extraction, including crawlers, scripts and repeated programmed requests even from a subscribed account; sets per-account daily document and request limits; prohibits account sharing; and reserves enforcement rights. The current public search route exposes civil and criminal judgment/principle categories, including labour appeals, and advanced search by keyword, year and circuit: https://cc.gov.eg/judgments_search/. For Legal Copilot, treat this as a manual lookup/link-out source only. No extraction or product reuse is authorized by the public search page. Rights-context note: WIPO Lex's consolidated record for Egyptian Law No. 82/2002, Article 141, excludes official court judgments from copyright protection but preserves protection for creative collections/selection/arrangement (https://www.wipo.int/wipolex/ar/legislation/details/22066). Article 141 does not override the Court's published access/use conditions or the explicit commercial written-approval requirement.

sources.authority: Supreme Constitutional Court of Egypt
sources.access_status: official public portal and recent-judgments page located; an independent third-party fetcher describes unauthenticated JSON API routes, but API availability, response completeness and terms were not independently validated
sources.permission_evidence: The official SCC portal page https://www.sccourt.gov.eg/newportal/?a=cp3&id=829 publicly displays recent judgments with case number, judicial year, date and short disposition summaries; the indexed sample includes judgments dated 9 September 2026. A 2019 State Information Service report describes a central SCC database containing 7,112 judgments from 1970–2018 and 8,225 cases. Separately, an independent third-party repository (worldwidelaw/legal-sources, sources/EG/SCC) documents a proposed fetcher for JSON routes `/DjangoPortal/api/Cases/get-cases-basedon-casestatuscode` and `/DjangoPortal/api/RulesInsert/get-rule-details-by-case-id`, and claims approximately 9,190 records across constitutional, legislative-interpretation and jurisdictional-conflict case types. That count and API behavior are third-party claims only: the endpoints were not successfully independently validated in this review, the official Court's own API documentation/terms were not located, and the fetched content/record-level citations are not established. The 2019 report's 7,112 count and the third-party 9,190 count refer to different reported snapshots and must not be conflated. Public availability does not establish permission for automated retrieval, local preservation, indexing, commercial display or redistribution. In a 2026-10-31 browser inspection, the official recent-judgments page title resolved but exposed no readable body text to the research viewer; therefore no individual judgment page or full-text sample was independently captured in that inspection. This is a limitation of the inspection method, not evidence that the portal lacks public content.
sources.bulk_download_or_api: An unauthenticated JSON API is described by an independent fetcher, but was not independently validated and no official bulk/API permission was identified. Do not call endpoints or bulk collect pending terms and rights review.

sources.authority: Egyptian Court of Cassation / Supreme Judicial Council
material_types: historical Court of Cassation and other court judgments
historical legal indexes and foreign-language summaries
sources.access_status: official heritage catalogue and individual document pages located under /heritage/documents/{id}; page-reader route located under /heritage/books/{id}/read; public browsing with original page images and watermark/no-republication notice; no bulk API/export established
sources.permission_evidence: The Court of Cassation's official announcement dated 26 August 2026 says its Legal Heritage Library became publicly available on 24 August 2026. It reports 27 scanned volumes, 13,275 scanned pages, 3,533 indexed documents and 12,577 index entries, covering 1899–1933 and documents from 316 courts/agencies. It describes original printed pages as browsable page-by-page, with judgment-level pages showing court, hearing date, cited provisions and printed principles. It says original text is transcribed verbatim in historical orthography and uncertain readings are flagged for review. It also explicitly says images carry a watermark to protect the originals from republication. This is strong primary-source discovery and a verification route, not a licence to copy, scrape, bulk-download, redistribute, or train on the scans. No reuse licence or API was identified. Direct public record routes were subsequently located: https://cc.gov.eg/heritage/documents/199 (1899 judgment, printed pages 120–129), https://cc.gov.eg/heritage/documents/5479 (1933 Court of Cassation and Appeal judgment, printed page 274), https://cc.gov.eg/heritage/documents/6018 (1936 first-year Al-Mohami legal periodical article), and https://cc.gov.eg/heritage/documents/25052 (1937 Court of Cassation judgment). These examples demonstrate searchable individual records and that the catalogue may expose related material beyond the 1899–1933 core volume range; preserve each record's own date/series metadata and do not infer coverage from the announcement alone. The catalogue search page is https://cc.gov.eg/judgments_search/ for current civil/criminal principles and rulings, but its reuse terms are separately unknown. A public book-reader page is also indexed at https://cc.gov.eg/heritage/books/31/read; this is an observed page instance, not a documented API or bulk-download route.
sources.bulk_download_or_api: not established; use public browsing only and respect watermark/no-republication statement
sources.required_next_action: Use individual public record pages for manual primary-source verification of historical citations and pinpoint references. Do not scrape, bulk download, remove watermarks, republish images, or ingest scans until explicit collection and commercial reuse permissions are established. Preserve printed volume/page references and mark uncertain readings exactly as the Court does. Treat the announced 1899–1933 heritage collection, the 1936 historical periodical and any later surfaced records as distinct series with record-specific dates. Keep current judgments search and heritage scans under separate source records if their access or terms differ.

sources.permission_evidence: The public dataset card declares an MIT license and says the corpus contains 2,434 Arabic legal-text records with 25,054,372 tokens. The visible schema contains law_name, categories, text and tokens; no record-level source URL, publication date, Gazette issue/page, effective date, amendment status or reviewer field is documented. The dataset's own description says texts were extracted from official Egyptian legal documents, but does not identify an upstream source or chain of rights for each record. Public preview samples include broad compilations such as قوانين الأحوال الشخصية, القرارات الوزارية الخاصة بالجمارك and موسوعة المواعيد, rather than only individually identified statutes; some visible text prefixes appear to contain extraction/noise artifacts. An independent fetcher description for this dataset maps every record to the same dataset homepage URL and sets date=null, confirming that it cannot provide source-level citation provenance as-is. The MIT declaration is evidence of the dataset publisher's stated license for the dataset package, not proof that every underlying legal text, third-party compilation, editorial material or source-derived database is covered by rights the publisher can grant. No records were downloaded or ingested in this review.
